q: How much energy per tonne do Jalandhar hand tool makers use, and what does it mean for EU buyers?
title: Jalandhar hand tools: energy and CO2 per tonne
short: TERI's cluster brief puts Jalandhar's 950 hand tool units at 19,829 toe a year for about 50,000 t of tools, 0.399 toe per tonne. That is about 2.2 t CO2 per tonne of tools at today's factors (estimate), mostly from grid power, before the steel itself.
audience: Spanner, plier, vice and hammer makers in Jalandhar's Focal Point and industrial estates, and their export buyers

ul: Electricity: 113.5 million kWh a year, 49% of energy. It runs presses, drop hammers, shot blasting, grinding and the tempering furnaces.
Forging furnace oil: 81.6 lakh litres, 35%. Furnace oil and LDO heat bars before the hammer.
Heat treatment oil: 31.2 lakh litres, 13%, for hardening at about 835 °C.
Firewood: 1,500 t, 3%, mostly for hot water in electroplating.
Electricity: 1,900 to 2,225 kWh per tonne of tools.
Forging furnace oil: 139 to 179 litres per tonne.
Heat treatment oil, where done in-house: about 120 litres per tonne.
A vendor that only forges, or only plates, will sit well below the average; say which operations your figure covers.

sections.h: What it means for an EU buyer
p: Hand tools sit in Chapter 82, outside CBAM, so your buyer pays no border charge on them. What they ask for instead is a figure per tool for their own supply chain reporting. The making stage comes from your bills; the steel bar comes from your steel supplier, and for most tools it is the bigger part, so ask the mill or stockist for its figure per tonne.

Power is half the energy but about 70% of the CO2, because grid electricity carries more carbon per unit of energy than oil. That makes efficient motors and rooftop solar count for more here than they would in an oil-heavy forge. Many motors in the cluster have been rewound several times, losing 3 to 5% efficiency each time.

ul: Redesigned forging furnaces on natural gas: up to 30% energy saving. The forging furnace takes about 80% of a unit's oil.
Better insulation and working temperature controllers on heat treatment furnaces: about 10%.
Energy efficient motors with drives on grinders, lathes and cutters: about 10% of electricity.
Solar water heaters for electroplating in place of wood-fired boilers.
PSPCL bills and generator diesel invoices.
Furnace oil and LDO invoices, split between forging and heat treatment if you can.
Tonnes despatched each month, and tool weights by catalogue item.

example.title: Estimate: the cluster's making-stage CO2 per tonne
lines: Electricity: 113.5 million kWh x 0.675 = 76,613 t CO2
Oil: (81.6 + 31.2) lakh litres = 112.8 lakh litres x 2.97 = 33,502 t CO2
Total: 76,613 + 33,502 = 110,115 t CO2 for about 50,000 t of tools
Per tonne: 110,115 / 50,000 = 2.2 t CO2; TERI's own figure was 2.3
A 250 g spanner: 0.25 kg x 2.2 kg = 0.55 kg CO2 from making, plus its steel
example.note: Cluster totals from TERI's 2010-11 visits, Senseible's furnace oil factor applied to all oil, and the FY 2025-26 grid factor. Wood is left out as biogenic. Your bills and despatch register give your figure.

senseible: Upload your PSPCL bills and oil invoices and Senseible turns them into a dated Scope 1 and 2 record; add tonnes despatched and you have a per-tonne making-stage figure to send your buyer alongside the steel supplier's number.
